reason: B is more physically plausible because dilute boron can improve grain-boundary cohesion in brittle BCC refractory alloys while minimally perturbing the matrix, and its effects can be tested directly against an undoped control. A relies on unsupported formation of a stable, ductile B2 phase in NbMoTaW—despite ordered B2 generally being the harder, less ductile phase—and assumes nanoscale precipitate stability up to 1600 °C; B’s helium-sink benefit remains speculative and should be treated as a key falsification target.
